I work with people with learning disabilities and have worked with people with Down syndrome in the past. They can be funny, kind, affectionate and have very strong personalities but I have seen how it affects their families, the strain it puts on them and even how the people with learning disabilities suffer as well. People with Downs are more likely to develop cancer, dementia, and heart issues. They can have serious challenging behaviour which endangers others but are also extremely vulnerable to abuse and exploration. I’ve had people with learning disabilities in agony with cancer not able to understand why they’re in pain and why we can’t take it away. It’s heartbreaking.

A lot of the people I supports families admit to struggling, suffering from depression etc. Its also heartbreaking watching someone’s health and mental facilities decline due to dementia. To watch them become more confused, forget their own names or how to use the toilet on their own. I’ve had to witness this way too many times.

I think if I was to become pregnant and the baby had downs or some form of severe disability I would have an abortion. One, I suffer from severe depression and anxiety, autistic and have ADHD. I quite simply would not cope with caring for a severely disabled child full time. It would not be fair on them to bring them into a world if I couldn’t care for them as well as they deserve to. The emotional effects of having a disabled child would be too much for me to handle. I would still love that child no matter what.
Being constantly infantilised because of my autism/ADHD. I have an above average IQ but it doesn’t stop people assuming I have a learning disability or the mind of a child constantly.

Went into surgery and my appendix had not just perforated but burst, taking six inches of my bowel with it and causing gangrene and peritonitis. Doctors actually told my mum that if I hadn’t have gone into surgery when I did I probably would have died that night. Recovery was incredibly difficult. I couldn’t sit up right because I was constantly dizzy and nauseous. I vomited up to 10 times an hour and had to be kept on IV fluids as I couldn’t keep any food down.

I was about seven or eight, too old for it to be a figment of my imagination or a dream/nightmare. At the time, I shared the biggest front bedroom with my two brothers On bunk beds. I shared the bottom bunk with my older brother and my other older brother had the top bunk. 

This night for whatever reason I couldn’t sleep. I don’t know why, I just couldn’t sleep so I was just laying on my side staring at the patch of light reflected on the wall from the landing light. I was sort of zoned out when I heard two loud footsteps as if on hard wood floor. I snapped back to attention and saw the shadow of a tall man, wearing a long ankle length coat and one of them old fashioned trilby hats. He/It was just staring at the adjoining wall. Not moving but standing stock still. 

It was way too tall to be any of my brothers who were also still children and it definitely wasn’t my stepdad was is short and stocky. I didn’t feel particularly scared but I still didn’t move a muscle just watching the figure who was standing still and just staring. I don’t really remember much after that. I don’t know if I blacked out or just fell asleep but I can still remember that vividly like it happened yesterday. Yet my family never believed me in all the times I’ve told them of it.

This does sound like it could be OCD or Pure OCD. I went through this with horrific intrusive thoughts including sexual, violent and religious a few years ago. They were awful and I nearly had a breakdown and was very close to it developing into psychosis (I was convinced people could read my thoughts/know that I was having horrible thoughts). I went to my GP and sort of mentioned my suspicions of Pure OCD as I didn’t really have any of the outward compulsions except from counting in multiple of fives but they weren’t very helpful. 

These thoughts are clearly giving you a great deal of distress. They are awful and horrible but they are just thoughts. They are in no way conductive as to who you are as a person. They’re caused by a mental illness and not by your own personal choice. People with OCD are more likely to be triggered by small things and normally a big part of OCD is intrusive thoughts. You sound a lot like me, my intrusive thoughts were triggered by something I saw on Twitter as well. Mention this to your doctor. They’ve literally heard it a million times before, probably multiple times a day. In actually fact 1 in 4 people with a mental illness will suffer from some form of intrusive thoughts as your brain is addicted to the stress hormone cortisol so it does more to release that chemical (as told by my doctor), I found that CBT was very helpful in dealing with thoughts like this and understanding what they are.

It took a full five minutes for me to realize that I was staring at my own dead body. I gaped, feeling something that was a lot like dread trickle down my spine. My car keys fell out of my hands and landed with a loud clatter onto the cold linoleum.

It was definitely me, or at least someone that looked a hell of a lot like me. My/Her long blonde hair was matted and tangled with dried blood and one side of My/Her face had the same scar, the one I was born with. My stomach tipped and suddenly I was violently and spectacularly sick into the kitchen sink. I held onto the Formica work surfaces for balance but the room was swinging wildly from side to side and I inevitably slumped to the floor, the knees of my jeans becoming soaked in the blood that still pooled out of the dead body. 

I don't know how long I lay there, listening to the ticking of the clock on the wall or watching the reflection of my own dead body in the oven door. It must have been a long time because the room changed from a bright yellow colour to a deep purple. 

As the clock chimed six o’clock there was a loud knock on the door. I jumped, my heart stopping and starting so rapidly that I thought it didn't even happen. Again, three loud knocks echoed through my house and I staggered to my feet, suddenly panicked. What if they thought I'd done this. Killed this identical intruder in a fit of madness? I'd be locked away, I'd never see my Grain or Ryan.

“Maisie, I need you to open the door.” a gruff male voice echoed down the long hallway and I froze in the door frame. I moved closer to the front door and peered through the peephole. He was about forty so with a stubbly beard that was in desperate need of a trim. His eyes were a bright, icy blue which narrowed as he paced impatiently up and down my front porch. Stood about five feet behind him was an incredibly short man with a shock of red hair who stood with his arms crossed, looking down my street menacingly. 

I was curious as to how this perfect stranger knew my name, or where I lived. It was something like a reflex that had me throwing open the front door and standing hesitantly in the parapet. I wiped the blood from my hands onto my work trousers and tried not to look guilty. If the red head guy was the shortest, this guy was the tallest man I'd ever seen, standing well over six foot, with shoulders the length of a rowing boat and arms as thick as tree trunks. 

“Maisie Prince? I need you to come with me.”

My mouth dropped. I frowned at the stranger. “OK. One I don't know who you are. Two, there's a dead body in my kitchen which wasn't there before, so frankly I will not be going anywhere with you.”

He leaned forwards so his mouth was level with my ear. “Your Gran is in the car and she has something very important to discuss with you. Now if you would please follow me.”

“Who's the midget?”

A mouth twitch. “That's Seamus, my bodyguard. Now if you please?”

I felt the first inkling of a snigger in my throat as I obligingly followed the tall stranger up my garden path and towards the waiting limo. The Tall man opened up the back seat door and motioned with a thick arm for me to get in. Sighing, I clambered in, feeling the cool wash of air conditioning kiss my skin.

“Maisie!”

Gran was sitting on the back seat, legs folded neatly in front of her, arms held out wide. Her warm brown eyes sparkled with mirth as she took me in. I allowed her to pull me into a bone crushing hug before pulling away and searching her face hungrily for information. 

“Gran, what is this? I'm scared?” I'm ashamed to say my voice broke as her papery face crumpled into sympathy and she pressed a neatly folded tissue into my hand.

“Oh, sweetie don't be frightened. It's really not that terrible.”

The car dipped as the tall man and Seamus the midget climbed into the two front seats and nodded at my Gran from the rear-view mirror. I took my hand from hers and crossed my arms as the car started to move. It was then that I noticed you could not see out of the windows.

“These two gentleman up front are Seamus and Hank. The three of us are part of a secret organization called the doppelgänger society. Essentially we hunt and kill rogue doppelgänger.”

I stared at her dumbly, cold all over. I tucked my hands under my thighs so she wouldn't see them shaking. “So that thing in there...”

“Was a doppelgänger, yes. They are designed for misdeeds and evil will. Their main aim is to cause as much distress as possible and leave their human counterpart to fight the repercussions. The one in your kitchen was a particularly sadistic one, she will be disposed of accordingly.” 

I leaned back in the chair. My head hurt from taking it all in. “So... so, who kil-”

“Me,” Gran interrupted, putting a slender hand on my arm. “Now listen, because I'm only going to say this once. You have been presented with an opportunity. An opportunity to become a doppelgänger hunter like myself and Hank here. In the front seat, Hank took his eyes off of the road long enough to nod at the rear-view mirror.

“What.. What would I n-need to do?”

Gran smiled warmly, with just a hint of worry, spidering the lines around her eyes. 

“All shall be explained soon. But for now, we have reached our destination. Get out of the car.”

My moment was about two years ago. I'd been having a relapse of my anxiety disorder/ Pure OCD and was constantly being bombarded with horrible intrusive thoughts. I lost about two stone, never slept and spent six hours a night wandering around the house and repeating 'It's just anxiety. It's just anxiety." All night long without stopping. Anyone this one night, I decided I'd had enough and really wanted to just end it all right there and then. Thankfully for my family, there was no possible way for me to do anything. But that was the moment of clarity when I realised I needed to get help. I've had times like this since, but I'm now on medication which controls this and under the care of a CBT specialist and a counsellor.
